title: Make the reminder letter safe on every server and for every note

blocks.text: The billing job sends a payment reminder for every unpaid invoice, and a copy of each letter goes to the payment portal, which reads the invoice line and expects the amount as digits, a dot and two decimals. The job runs on servers in Dublin and in Frankfurt. Two incidents came in this month:

items: every letter sent from Frankfurt was rejected by the portal;
the job stopped halfway through one night's run, on a customer whose account manager had left a note on the invoice.

blocks.text: `ReminderLetter` already holds the letter's template, `LETTER`. Write `render(Invoice)` in `src/main/java/practice/ReminderLetter.java` so that the letter is the same wherever the job runs, and any note the account manager writes appears as its own last line, exactly as written. About five lines in total.

cases.says: an invoice without a note gets the two lines of the letter, filled in
an account manager's note becomes a third line after the invoice line
on a server whose default locale is German the amount still has a dot before its two decimals
a note containing a percent sign is copied into the letter as written

origin.section: formatted() Is String.format With the Default Locale, and Every % Is a Specifier

concepts: formatted() is String.format with the default locale, so machine-read text needs String.format with an explicit locale.
Every % in a template starts a specifier, so a literal percent sign is %% and data goes in as an argument, never into the template.
